register.name: Government Development Bonds and domestic sovereign sukuk, 2026 borrowing plan
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · State General Budget 2026 · development bonds of RO 150M a quarter and domestic sukuk of RO 125M in the first and third quarters · 84th development bond issue: seven years at 4.5%, issue date 25 August 2026
register.note: The Central Bank of Oman issues the bonds on behalf of the Government; proceeds of the 84th issue go to general budgetary purposes
register.text: The domestic borrowing of the Government of Oman for 2026: RO 600 million in Government Development Bonds and RO 250 million in domestic sovereign sukuk, part of a plan that covers a budget deficit of RO 530 million with net borrowing of RO 130 million and RO 400 million drawn from reserves. It finances the public budget as a whole; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Social protection benefits, State General Budget 2026
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · State General Budget 2026 · 1,627,365 beneficiaries expected in 2026
register.note: The Social Protection Fund reported 1,552,749 active beneficiaries of social protection benefits at the end of January 2026
register.text: The 2026 state budget allocates RO 614 million to social protection benefits, which the Social Protection Fund pays to older people, children, persons with disabilities, orphans and widows, and as family income support. It finances the livelihood standard directly, for about 1.6 million beneficiaries expected in 2026.

register.name: International sovereign sukuk (4.525%)
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · 7.5 years · annual coupon 4.525% · 60 basis points over US Treasuries · reported in the fiscal performance bulletin for the third quarter of 2025
register.note: RO 385 million; alongside, a buyback of RO 117 million of Eurobonds maturing in June 2026 and a partial repayment of international sukuk maturing in October 2025
register.text: A US$1 billion international sukuk of the Government of Oman, issued as it bought back part of its Eurobonds due in June 2026 and repaid part of its international sukuk due in October 2025. It refinances the public finances as a whole; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Climate Resilience Flood Protection Dams Project
register.detail: Islamic Development Bank · OMN1028 · installment sale · signed in Algiers, May 2025, at the 50th IsDB Group Annual Meeting · Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources
register.note: The Minister of Finance signed agreements worth RO 243 million with the IsDB Group for climate-resilient flood protection dams
register.text: IsDB financing for four flood protection dams, on Wadi Al Khoud in Seeb, Wadi Rijma in Liwa, Wadi Majlas in Qurayat and Wadi Ahin in Saham, with Saham Agriculture City and a centre for institutional development and capacity building. It protects communities from flash floods, serving the shelter, water and food standards.

register.name: Ibri III Solar Independent Power Project
register.detail: Masdar, Korea Midland Power, Al Khadra Partners and OQ Alternative Energy · financial close 16 January 2026 · lenders Natixis CIB and First Abu Dhabi Bank · offtaker Nama Power and Water Procurement · 500 MW solar with 100 MWh battery storage
register.note: Total project cost of around US$300 million; the debt amount is not disclosed; expected to power around 33,000 homes
register.text: Debt financing for the first utility-scale solar and battery storage project in Oman, a 500 MW photovoltaic plant with a 100 MWh battery, built to sell its power to Nama Power and Water Procurement. It adds clean power for around 33,000 homes and avoids about 505,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide a year, serving the energy standard.

register.name: Sustainable financing for National Finance Company
register.detail: IFC · signed 14 April 2025 in Muscat at the World Bank Group joint meeting with the Ministry of Finance · up to $120M
register.note: IFC signed two further agreements the same day: with Future Fund Oman, and for the United Solar Polysilicon plant in Sohar
register.text: IFC financing of up to US$120 million to National Finance Company, a leading finance company in Oman, to widen access to sustainable finance for its retail and small and medium-sized enterprise clients and to support clean transport, renewable energy and energy and water efficiency. It serves the livelihood and energy standards.
